stories.title: Former City lawyer raises $2.2m for AI startup to speed up private capital deals
stories.ltme_summary: London legal AI startup Perry AI has raised $2.2m in a seed round led by Haatch, with Antler, Syncorp Ventures and Araya Ventures also taking part, according to the company. Founded by former funds lawyers Shashwat Patel and Vaneesa Agrawal, the platform helps private equity and venture capital firms manage fund obligations. Perry AI says the money will fund expansion into the US and Asia. The company also claims deal signing times can fall from 84 days to 13 days.

He told the committee the Solicitors Regulation Authority had been left with a bloody nose after repeated failed cases, and called for due diligence duties before litigation. The article is about legal regulation rather than technology.
stories.hook: RPC's Rupert Cowper-Coles tells MPs the SRA has taken a bloody nose over SLAPPs

stories.title: Denigration of lawyers is 'step towards authoritarianism'

Speakers including Natasha Williams and Jacqueline McKenzie described threats to lawyers in the UK and Belarus. The Law Society's vice president urged the UK to ratify the 2025 Council of Europe Convention on the Protection of the Lawyer.
stories.hook: UN rapporteur Margaret Satterthwaite links attacks on lawyers to authoritarian drift

stories.title: Smaller tribunal panels could speed up 'timelines', consultation suggests

The open tribunal caseload reached 887,000 at the end of June 2026, up 16 per cent. Any change needing a new practice direction would not take effect before April 2027. The consultation closes on 25 January 2027.
stories.hook: Tribunals consult on smaller panels as open caseload hits 887,000

MPs call for national legal service to improve access to justice
stories.ltme_summary: The justice select committee's access to legal services report calls for a national legal service to coordinate advice, modelled on NHS 111, and for legal regulation reform. It also backs an interest on lawyers' client accounts scheme in principle, but not as the Ministry of Justice proposed. The report urges AI-assisted public legal information, with a public information repository to reduce hallucination risk.
stories.hook: MPs urge a national legal service and AI-assisted legal support platform for access to justice

stories.title: Justice committee backs major legal regulation reform
stories.ltme_summary: The House of Commons justice committee says the regulatory framework for legal services does not serve access to justice and needs a new settlement. MPs back a single regulator model, endorsing Professor Stephen Mayson's proposal, and flag the use of technology by unregulated providers and weak oversight by the Legal Services Board. The report follows the 2026 public bodies review.
stories.hook: MPs say legal services regulation must be fundamentally reviewed and possibly consolidated

Published research describes four unbundling models and says the BSB is discussing a shared definition of unbundled services with other legal regulators. It will consider further guidance on working with third-party platforms.
stories.hook: BSB says barristers are well placed for unbundled work on third-party legal platforms

stories.hook: Justice committee chair Catherine Atkinson backs an NHS 111-style National Legal Service
